title: Microsoft Project Review (2026)
intro: Microsoft Project is evaluated here as a spreadsheet-style / PMO work management platform — Microsoft Project (with Planner) is the Microsoft 365 project-management ladder for task boards, Gantt schedules, resource management and portfolio views. Common published floors: Planner Plan 1 ~$10/user/mo; Planner and Project Plan 3 ~$30; Plan 5 ~$55 (availability for new customers can change). Best for organisations already standardised on Microsoft 365 — landscape as traditional/enterprise PMO rather than a modern Work OS peer. This review uses SoftwareGlimpse’s project-management methodology (ease of use, work planning, automation, collaboration, integrations, reporting, scalability, value, AI), scoring products inside their job cluster rather than against unrelated peers. It is based on first-party research, not hands-on lab testing.
summary: Choose Microsoft Project/Planner when Microsoft 365 is the system of work and traditional scheduling/portfolio depth matters — landscape on modern Work OS lists.
verdict: Choose Microsoft Project/Planner when Microsoft 365 is the system of work and traditional scheduling/portfolio depth matters — landscape on modern Work OS lists. Compare Smartsheet for spreadsheet PMO, monday/Asana for modern Work OS, and Jira for engineering delivery. Scores reflect first-party documentation as of 2026-08-17 — not hands-on product testing. Confirm current packaging, minimums and usage rates on the vendor site before purchase.

criterionAssessments.rationale: Familiar inside M365 but classic Project scheduling has a learning curve vs Asana.
Gantt, dependencies and resource scheduling are a traditional PM strength — 9.
Power Automate helps; native PM automation thinner than ClickUp/monday.
Teams/M365 collaboration is strong when the org is already there.
Deepest Microsoft ecosystem story in this category set — 9.
Solid project/portfolio reporting on higher plans.
Enterprise PMO scale path via Plan 3/5.
Plan 3/5 seats are premium vs modern Work OS floors; value depends on M365 standardisation. Affiliate economics excluded.
Copilot-adjacent AI may apply via M365 — not Motion-class product AI.

bestFor: Enterprise portfolio planning on higher plans
notIdealFor: Startups wanting modern Work OS UX
cons: Not a modern Work OS peer
limitations: SKU and licensing complexity across Planner/Project plans
Classic Project UX steeper than modern Work OS tools
Plan 5 new-customer availability should be confirmed live
pricingSummary: Planner Plan 1 ~$10; Plan 3 ~$30; Plan 5 ~$55 per user/mo (medium). Confirm live M365 SKUs.

faq.question: Is Microsoft Project a project management / work OS tool?
faq.answer: No. Microsoft Project is an adjacent desktop workspace organizer. It wraps web apps into desktop shells — it is not a project tracker or work OS.

faq.question: How is Microsoft Project priced?
faq.answer: Planner Plan 1 ~$10; Plan 3 ~$30; Plan 5 ~$55 per user/mo (medium). Confirm live M365 SKUs.

faq.question: Does Microsoft Project have a free plan or free trial?
faq.answer: No free plan is published. A free trial is documented. Confirm current terms with the vendor.

faq.question: Did SoftwareGlimpse personally test Microsoft Project?
faq.answer: No. This review is based on first-party product and pricing research evidence, not hands-on product usage. Affiliate relationships never influence scores.
